items.verified: The original walker selected chain_seq > cursor and omitted NULL sequences. SQLite cap insertion relied on trigger reentry.
items.change: Detect NULL/nonpositive sequences, count/link/head mismatches; export only positive chained sequences; explicitly seal SQLite siem.gap rows without nested triggers.
items.tests: NULL-sequence refusal and exclusion after recording; real cap event with recursive_triggers=OFF; concurrent raw/ORM appends.

items.verified: Retention materialized all expired rows and one expanding ID list. Erasure held all preimages and one user-sized IN list.
items.change: Retention uses indexed 256-row sequence pages and range deletes. Erasure spools private preimages and writes 256-row receipt batches atomically.
items.tests: 512-bind ceiling on 1,200 target rows; 70,001-row erasure and 300,001-row retention; remaining chain verifies.

items.verified: The walker returned at the first break, rejected invalid-before checkpoints immediately, and alerts compared only first_break.
items.change: Continue through every break, assign stable fingerprints, retain authenticated known breaks, alert on any new fingerprint, include known breaks in signed export manifests and the UI.
items.tests: Later corruption produces a second alert despite the same first row; invalid-before receipt/checkpoint traversal; signed known-break exports; UI lists all breaks.

items.verified: Receipt HMACs used JWT_SECRET_KEY without a key identifier.
items.change: Separate mode-0600 .audit-hmac-keys.json, atomic creation/rotation, key IDs on signed evidence, retired keys retained. Updated SECRET_ROTATION.md.
items.tests: JWT changes leave receipts valid; audit-key rotation and module reload preserve old verification; key bytes absent from SQLite.

items.verified: Full walks compared only database state and did not confirm the previous signed head. Missing status read pending.
items.change: Persist an authenticated head outside the database, check it on walks, carry its hash through retention checkpoints, and report attention for missing/unauthentic status or external continuity evidence.
items.tests: Rehashed replacement chain; missing/forged status; changed status timestamp; missing external head; head inside a retained range.

items.verified: Positive audit retention values below 90 were accepted and used unchanged.
items.change: Licensed audit integrity requires at least 90 days; zero retains forever. Reject shorter writes and clamp older saved policies at read/cleanup after upgrade. Documented in UI and operator guide.
items.tests: Tier/zero/boundary checks and real GET/PUT/cleanup routes keep 30-day rows while deleting 100-day rows under an old one-day policy.

items.verified: The SQLite UDF called get_license (identity/license reads), SQLite wrote siem_until, syslog reused sockets without close detection and ignored the CA, daily checks lacked a worker lock, and the binding comment was displaced.
items.change: Use cached signed license with an in-memory expiry check and fail-closed UDF; write siem_until only on PostgreSQL; one-event syslog connections with read-ahead and custom TLS CA; installation file lock across workers; remove unused imports and restore binding_protocol comment at its model.
items.tests: No trigger license refresh, expiry/failure/lapse handling, no SQLite deadline write, retained outbox on socket close, TLS CA/reconnect mocks, and a separate-process lock test.

limitations: Sandbox denies owned loopback listeners. Blocked cases remain failures/errors in raw pytest XML, never passes.
Native PostgreSQL cases remain environment-gated. PostgreSQL 18 is a separately headed pre-existing follow-up and was not changed in this E1 review.
Syslog TCP has no receiver application ACK. Read-ahead detects observed close; success cannot prove durable receiver storage.
All changed code/source files are below 700 lines. Existing CHANGELOG and generated inventory/frozen ORM JSON data remain longer; comments, history and pinned data are preserved.
The exhaustive restore-ledger test now caches each integrity-validated frozen ledger once per routing test, retaining all real/future prefix assertions. Production validation is unchanged.
No git commit, push, deployment, paid API call, or external SIEM configuration was performed. Independent Claude review of this revised diff remains a handoff step.
